content.user_title: Run Project Lint and Type Checks
content.value_statement: Developers need a consistent way to verify code before handoff. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through project linting and typechecking commands.
actual_capabilities: Lists ESLint commands for linting selected files.
Lists a TypeScript no-emit typecheck command.
Names common lint and type errors to resolve.
Documents Bash as the required tool interface.
limitations: Does not define a complete custom lint configuration.
Requires project dependencies and toolchains to be installed.
Uses example commands that may need project-specific replacement.
Does not verify test execution beyond lint and typecheck.

use_cases.title: Validate Feature Changes
use_cases.description: Run lint and typecheck commands before submitting implementation work.

use_cases.title: Review Code Quality
use_cases.description: Check common lint, import order, unused variable, and type issues during review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Checks
use_cases.description: Give assistants a shared validation workflow for local development tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Lint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the lint skill to check the files I changed and summarize any issues found.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Safe Auto-Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the lint skill to apply safe lint auto-fixes, then report any remaining issues.

prompt_templates.title: Lint and Typecheck
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the lint skill to lint my changed paths, run the typecheck, and separate lint issues from type errors.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Failed Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the lint skill to investigate failed validation, identify likely causes, and propose minimal fixes.

output_examples.input: User asks to lint changed TypeScript files.
output: Runs the configured lint command on provided paths.
Reports unused variables and import order findings.
Suggests safe fixes or asks before applying changes.

output_examples.input: User asks for a typecheck before handoff.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs the configured no-emit typecheck, summarizes errors by file, and identifies the first fixes to make.

output_examples.input: User asks to auto-fix lint issues.
output: Applies the configured auto-fix command to selected files.
Summarizes changed files and remaining manual work.

best_practices: Run lint before and after auto-fix to confirm remaining issues.
Limit file arguments to paths from the current trusted workspace.
Run typecheck after lint fixes because changes can reveal type issues.
anti_patterns: Do not run auto-fix across unrelated files without user approval.
Do not paste untrusted paths directly into shell commands.
Do not treat lint success as full test coverage.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on linting, auto-fix, and typechecking workflows.

faq.question: Can it fix lint issues automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents an ESLint auto-fix workflow for selected files.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it need project dependencies installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The workspace must provide the lint and typecheck tools.

faq.question: Can the commands be changed?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill uses examples that maintainers can replace with project-specific commands.

faq.question: Is it safe for any repository?
faq.answer: Use it only in trusted workspaces because it asks assistants to run local development commands.
